reference.title: Scenario 21 — Nested Bullet List Between Numbered List in a Procedure
reference.shortdesc: Consider a procedure where a step's supporting bullet list itself contains a second, deeper level

section.p: Consider a procedure where a step's supporting bullet list itself contains a second, deeper level of nested bullets — for example, a general prerequisite item followed by a sub-list of specific requirements under one of its bullets.

row.entry: [Heading 2]:Prepare the Environment [List Number]:Verify the following prerequisites are met. [List Bullet]:Administrator access is available. [List Bullet]:Network requirements: [List Bullet, level 2]:Static IP address configured. [List Bullet, level 2]:Port 443 open for outbound traffic. [List Number]:Run the installer.

entry.codeblock:
Prepare the Environment Verify the following prerequisites are met.
  • Administrator access is available.
  • Network requirements:
    • Static IP address configured.
    • Port 443 open for outbound traffic.
 Run the installer.

section.p: Result: The converter preserves both bullet levels as supporting information rather than promoting either level to a procedural step. The mapping becomes:

ul.li: Second-level bullets → a nested <ul> inside the enclosing <li>

section.p: Similarly, consider a procedure where one of the selectable options itself carries a short explanatory sub-list — for example, clarifying what additional input or configuration a specific option requires, rather than introducing separate procedural steps or additional top-level choices.

row.entry: [Heading 2]:Select Installation Type [List Number]:Choose the installation type. [List Bullet]:Typical Installation [List Bullet]:Custom Installation [List Bullet, level 2]:Requires manual selection of components. [List Bullet, level 2]:Requires a target install path. [List Number]:Start the installation.

entry.codeblock:
Select Installation Type Choose the installation type. Typical Installation Custom Installation
  • Requires manual selection of components.
  • Requires a target install path.
 Start the installation.

section.p: Result: The converter preserves the outer bullet list as <choices>/<choice>because the items represent mutually exclusive, user-selectable options rather than plain descriptive bullets. The sub-bullets under Custom Installation are retained as a nested <ul> inside that specific <choice>, since they clarify a condition of that one option rather than introducing separate steps or additional top-level choices. The mapping becomes:

ul.li: The second-level <ul> stays nested inside its parent <choice>, scoped only to the option it clarifies
